response.reason: The skill contains only generic operational guidance for order-related actions (cancellation, modification, return/exchange), with no specific task IDs, named users, products, order numbers, addresses, or benchmark artifacts. It consistently defers to and operationalizes the native retail policy (status checks, once-per-order modify/exchange calls, single explicit confirmation before updates, one tool call at a time, closing summary after execution), and does not introduce hidden objectives or conflicting procedures.

The strategy avoids inventing facts and stays within scenario-provided identifiers, so factual truth and backend reality are preserved. However, it instructs the user to withhold subgoals, give terse confirmations, and deflect completeness checks, which conflicts with several scenario-specific requirements (e.g., not confirming until the smart watch and e-reader are included, mentioning all exchange items at the same time, and only exchanging the desk lamp on confirmation). This can lead to incomplete or incorrect actions, so the business objective is not preserved for every scenario.
